posts.body:
1.36 million people reached. Here's the number I stopped reporting.

Reach means an ad was shown to a screen. It costs nothing to grow and tells you nothing about money.

Across nine Meta ad accounts, in India, UK, US and Canada, I've generated 7,341 lead-form submissions and 876 conversations started from ads. Those numbers I still watch closely.

For a Tirupur apparel manufacturer, Nova Attire, one campaign set brought 4,248 wholesale buyer leads at ₹16.58 each, about 20 cents. Good cost. Real enquiries.

What we never captured: how many of those 4,248 became actual orders. That number was never sent back into Meta, so the system never learned what a real buyer looked like from a lead.

Reach would have made that campaign look even better than it already was.

If you're running ads and can only track one number properly, track the one after the lead: did it become money. Everything before that is context, not proof.

I put together a short audit checklist for exactly this — happy to share it if it's useful.

#advertising #meta #tirupur
warnings: UNVERIFIED: "one campaign set brought 4,248 wholesale buyer leads at ₹16.58 each, about 20 cents." — Approved facts state 4,248 leads came across six campaigns (3,585 in main account + 663 in second), not from 'one campaign set.'

check: "Under 20 cents an enquiry. On paper, one of the best-performing campaigns I've r" — Characterizing it as 'one of the best-performing campaigns' is an unsupported first-hand judgment/ranking not in approved facts; also repeats the single-campaign framing error.

check: "So the algorithm never learned what a real buyer looked like." — Presents a certain factual claim about how Meta's algorithm works/learns as established fact, which is a generalization beyond approved facts.
check: "Reach would have made that same campaign look even more impressive. It still wou" — Speculative claim about how reach would have appeared, not supported by approved facts.

check: "Reach means Meta showed your ad to a screen. Nobody promised a person read it." — Stated as certain fact/platform mechanic in a way that goes beyond simple well-known mechanics; borders on unsupported generalization.

slides.text: 1.36 million people reached. Taught me nothing.
Reach is the easiest number to buy and the emptiest one to report.
Reach means Meta showed your ad to a screen. Nobody promised a person read it.
Across nine ad accounts, in India, UK, US, Canada, I've collected 7,341 lead-form submissions.
876 of those turned into an actual conversation started from the ad. That's the number that matters more.
For Nova Attire, a Tirupur apparel manufacturer, one campaign set brought 4,248 wholesale buyer leads at ₹16.58 each.
Under 20 cents an enquiry. On paper, one of the best-performing campaigns I've run.
But nobody ever recorded how many of those 4,248 leads placed an order.
That number was never sent back into Meta. So the algorithm never learned what a real buyer looked like.
Reach would have made that same campaign look even more impressive. It still wouldn't know what sold.
The cheapest number to report is reach. The only one worth reporting is what came after the lead.
